description: You're scaling your Facebook ads wrong — and I can prove it. 🔥 Duplicating campaigns. Stacking audiences. Testing new ad sets. Every single one of those moves is costing you money. The gurus are teaching a system that worked 3 years ago. Meta doesn't need you to tell it who your customer is anymore. Still running interest-stacked campaigns? Drop a comment 👇 Comment "WAY" and I'll send you the link to the full episode where I walk through a real ad account using this exact scaling method. #FacebookAdsForFashion #MetaAdsStrategy #StopBoostingPosts #ClothingBrandOwner #BoutiqueOwner #FashionMarketing #ProfitableAds #ScaleYourBrand #AdsThatActuallyWork #FacebookAds #MetaAds #Profit #Facebook
transcript: You're scaling your Facebook ads wrong and I can prove it. So most clothing brands scaling ads right now are doing it by duplicating campaigns, messing with budgets, testing new audiences, and every single one of those moves is costing you money. So the gurus online are teaching a system that worked three years ago, five years ago, duplicate the ad set, test broad, scale the winner, run a testing campaign, and if it doesn't work, it must be your creative. No, the problem is the method. Meta doesn't need you to tell it who your customer is anymore. Meta's algorithm is smarter than any Interstac you're going to build. What Meta needs from you is a profitable offer and patience. Those who can spend the most to acquire customer will always win. I think that's a quote from Dan Kennedy, which is basically like, if you know your number so well that you can spend more than your competitors to acquire, you will get that customer. And as long as you can do it profitably down the line, you will continue to win. But you can only spend more when you actually know those numbers. And that's where we start.
